One sunny summer morning, Mother Duck sat on her nest by the pond.
Crack, crack, crack!
Out popped three fluffy yellow ducklings.
But the biggest egg did not crack at all.
At last the big egg went crack!
Out came a big grey duckling with a long neck and big flat feet.
Oh my, what a big baby!
said Mother Duck, and she tucked him under her wing.
Big or small, I love you all,
said Mother Duck.
The next morning Mother Duck led her babies down to the pond, one behind the other.
Paddle, paddle, splish, splash!
The big grey duckling swam the fastest of all.
On the bank the yellow ducklings looked at their big grey brother.
Dilly, the smallest, began to giggle.
Your neck is so long, and your feet are so big!
said Dilly.
You do not look like a duck at all.
The big grey duckling looked down at his feet.
He felt a little sad.
Mother Duck put her wing around him.
Dilly, that was not kind,
Everyone is different, and that is a good thing.
Dilly hung her head.
Sorry, big brother,
You are the best swimmer of us all.
But if I do not look like a duck, what kind of bird am I?
said Duckling.
Go and look around the farm, and you may find out,
Be home in time for supper.
So off he waddled across the meadow, waving goodbye.
In the farmyard a plump brown Hen was scratching for corn.
Am I a hen like you?
Cluck, cluck! Can you lay an egg?
said Hen.
Duckling shook his head.
Then you are not a hen,
said Hen, and she smiled.
But you are a very polite little bird.
Now run home for your supper.
Soon it was autumn, and the leaves turned red and gold.
One day three big white birds with long necks like his flew high over the pond.
Those are swans,
Am I a swan like you?
called Duckling.
But the swans were too high to hear him, and they flew far away.
Then winter came.
Snow fell softly, and the pond turned to ice.
Hen fluffed up her feathers at the barn door.
Come inside, all of you!
It is warm and dry in the barn.
So the ducks waddled through the snow, one behind the other, into the barn.
All winter long the ducks and Hen snuggled together in the soft, warm straw.
Duckling slept between Mother Duck and Dilly.
whispered Mother Duck.
At last spring came, and the ice melted away.
Duckling had grown big over the winter.
He went down to the pond and looked into the water.
There he saw a beautiful white bird with a long, graceful neck.
Is that really me?
Swoosh!
Three white swans glided down onto the pond and swam up to him.
Yes, you are!
said Swan, and he bowed his long neck.
You are a young swan, and a fine one.
Welcome, friend!
Mother Duck and the ducklings came paddling out to see.
Will you swim with my family too?
Of course,
said Swan.
The pond is big enough for everyone.
Ducks and swans swam round the pond together.
That evening the sun went down, pink and gold.
Dilly and the other ducklings rode home on their big brother's back.
You are a swan, and you are still our brother,
And Duckling was happier than he had ever been.
